goals.0: In Germany you have to register your address (usually within 14 days)
goals.1: Form words: Name, Vorname, Geburtsdatum, Staatsangehörigkeit, Familienstand
grammar.0.title: Common boxes on a form
grammar.0.note: On German forms „Name“ or „Nachname“ means the family name and „Vorname“ the first name. Decide in advance where each part of your name goes — and match your passport.
grammar.1.title: Anmeldung: what do you need?
grammar.1.note: Rule: you usually must register within 14 days of moving into a new home. You may need to book an appointment online beforehand — see your city's website. The Meldebescheinigung is needed for banks, jobs and renting.
grammar.1.rows.1.1: certificate from the landlord (that you live there)
grammar.2.title: Imperativ (Sie) at the office
grammar.2.text: „Füllen Sie das Formular aus.“ · „Unterschreiben Sie bitte hier.“ · „Warten Sie bitte im Flur.“ · „Bringen Sie alle Unterlagen mit.“ — the Sie imperative is a polite instruction: verb + Sie. The prefix of a separable verb goes at the end (füllen … aus).
quiz.1.why: ausfüllen = to fill in a form.
quiz.5.why: Sie imperative: the separable prefix goes at the end.
quiz.6.prompt: Within how many days must you do the Anmeldung?
quiz.8.prompt: What is the article of Unterschrift?
quiz.9.prompt: Put the sentence in order: “Please sign here.”
